prerequisites: Strength of Materials I and II

learning_outcomes.text: Possess knowledge about matrix and reinforcement materials of composites.
Know the production techniques of composite materials and produce them using basic methods.
Prepare experimental setups for composite structures and perform necessary tests.
Calculate the necessary Mechanical Properties in composite material determination using Theoretical and Analytical methods to obtain Elastic Constants.
Perform Stress-Strain calculations for composite structures.
Apply and calculate Yield and Fracture criteria for composites.

syllabus_topics: Classification of composites by matrix materials (Polymer Matrix Composites, Ceramic Matrix Composites, and Metal Matrix Composites)
Classification of composites by reinforcement elements (Fiber composites, Particulate composites, Laminated composites, and Hybrid composites)
Plastic Matrix materials (Polymers: Thermosets, Thermoplastics, and Elastomers)
Metal matrix materials (Aluminum, titanium, magnesium, etc.)
Application areas of composites and how to apply them

Introduction to mechanical behavior of composite materials (Elasticity; Calculation of Elastic Constants for Isotropic, Orthotropic and Anisotropic materials; Stress-Strain relationships; Stress Transformations; Layer Failure Criteria)
Experimental determination and calculation of mechanical properties
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by 60% of the in-year success and 40% of the final exam. The in-year success is calculated from a midterm exam (50%), two quizzes (15% each), homework (10%), and a performance task (laboratory) (10%).
